ca_stress_management_boulder.blurb: Stress Management Boulder is a single tall, cube-shaped block among the Emeralds boulders near Lake Tahoe, in forest just off Highway 20 at roughly 5,000 feet. The southwest side is the sunny one and holds the easier, lower-angle problems, while the other faces are harder. There are eight problems, running from VB up to V3, with most of them at V0 or below, so it works well for beginners and for warming up. The friction on the rock is good, and the way down is a downclimb on the shaded side.

ca_stealth_wall.blurb: Stealth Wall is a small crag at Donner Summit, on the Lake Tahoe side of the I-80 corridor, at about 6,700 feet. It faces southeast, so it is sunny from early in the day until the middle of the afternoon, and the walk from the road is short. The eight routes mix bolted lines with crack climbs: four sport, three trad and one that is set up for top rope. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.11, and half the routes sit in the 5.11 range, so it suits climbers who want a few moderate trad leads alongside harder sport pitches.

ca_top_hat.blurb: Top Hat is a backcountry crag in the Santa Monica Mountains, on a plateau above Circle X Ranch near Sandstone Peak and Mt. Olympus, at about 2,700 feet. Its oddly tilted summit blocks make it easy to recognize. Reaching the climbs means a fire-road hike from Mt. Olympus, a descent to a saddle and a scramble beside the big face to the summit formations. The eight routes are nearly all sport, with one that takes trad gear. Grades run from 5.9 to 5.12 and cluster around 5.11, so it suits climbers comfortable on bolted pitches in the harder 5.10s and up.

ca_star_wars_rock.blurb: Star Wars Rock is a large formation at the northern end of the Virgin Islands area in Joshua Tree National Park, within the Queen Valley area, and it is easy to pick out from the road. The rock is monzogranite, split by several crack lines, and one of its faces overhangs steeply. There are eight routes, nearly all trad, plus one top-rope line. Grades start with a 5.2 scramble and then jump to 5.9 and the 5.10s, with 5.10 the most common, finishing at 5.12. It suits climbers who can place their own gear on moderate to hard cracks.

_expect.name: West Nile Boulder (aka The Creek Boulder)

ca_west_nile_boulder_aka_the_creek_bould.blurb: West Nile Boulder, also known as the Creek Boulder, is in Rattlesnake Canyon in the Santa Barbara area, only about 100 feet up the trail from the trailhead at roughly 950 feet of elevation. The block hangs over the creekbed on the left of the path. It holds eight problems from V3 to V9, with six of them V5 or harder and two at V9, so it is a spot for stronger boulderers rather than a first-day warm-up, though one V3 is there for loosening up. The rock is sandstone.

ca_sundagger_wall.blurb: Sundagger Wall is in Valley of the Moon, in south San Diego County close to the Mexico border, at around 3,900 feet. It faces Patina Wall across a gully. The left side has a couple of long slab climbs, while a horizontal seam on the right cuts the wall in two and creates a ledge between the lower and upper routes. There are eight routes, seven of them sport and one a trad crack, graded 5.7 to 5.10 with 5.10 the most common. The rock is good quality, making it a reasonable pick for climbers working through the moderate sport grades.
